{{More citations needed|date=December 2025}}{{Short description|Mathematical constant}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Favard constant''' (also called the '''Akhiezer&ndash;Krein&ndash;Favard  constant''') of order <math> r </math> is defined as<ref name="finch">{{cite book
 | title = Mathematical Constants
 | first = Steven R. | last = Finch
 |author-link=Steven R. Finch
 | year = 2003
 | publisher = [[Cambridge University Press]]
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=Pl5I2ZSI6uAC&pg=PA256
 | page = 256
}}</ref>
<math display="block"> K_r = \frac{4}{\pi} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty} \left[ \frac{(-1)^k}{2k+1} \right]^{r+1}.</math>
The particular values of Favard constant are <math display="inline">K_0 = 1</math>, <math display="inline">K_1 = \frac{\pi}{2}</math>, <math  display="inline">K_2 = \frac{\pi^2}{8}</math>.{{r|finch}}

This constant is named after the French mathematician [[Jean Favard]], and after the  Soviet mathematicians [[Naum Akhiezer]] and [[Mark Krein]].

==Uses==
This constant is used in solutions of several extremal problems, for example

* Favard's constant is the sharp constant in [[Jackson's inequality]] for [[trigonometric polynomial]]s
* the sharp constants in the [[Landau–Kolmogorov inequality]] are expressed via Favard's constants
* Norms of periodic [[perfect spline]]s.
*The second Favard constant, <math>K_2 = \frac{\pi^2}{8} </math> is the same as the value of the internal 4-dimensional equivalent of the angles in a [[tesseract]]. The first Favard constant is equal to the value of the internal solid angles in cubes, and the internal angles in squares.{{cn|date=June 2025}}
